goal: Ensure private broadcast always completes all three initial connections, even if the transaction is received back early, closing timing attacks that could deanonymize the broadcaster.

result.summary: This PR reworks the private broadcast module so that all three initial connections for a privately broadcast transaction are always completed, rather than being cancelled early once the transaction is seen back on the network. It replaces the old Remove() semantics with MarkReceived(), adds explicit disconnect tracking (NodeDisconnected) and a TryGrantRetry mechanism to gate stale-tx retries, and adds a new functional test plus fuzz/unit test coverage for the new behavior.
result.problem: The current private broadcast logic can stop opening the remaining initial connections as soon as the transaction is seen returning from the network, which theoretically leaks timing information that could help an observer deanonymize the broadcasting node. This affects users relying on -privatebroadcast for transaction origin privacy.

result.card: This PR reworks Bitcoin Core's private broadcast module so all three initial connections for a privately-broadcast transaction always complete, even if the tx is seen back from the network early, closing a described theoretical timing attack that could help deanonymize the broadcaster. It is offered as an alternative to the already-open #34707 and also claims to fix related timing issues raised in review of #29415. The change touches net_processing.cpp and private_broadcast.{h,cpp}, replacing Remove() with MarkReceived(), adding NodeDisconnected() and TryGrantRetry(), plus new functional, fuzz, and unit tests. Discussion is minimal so far: a single Concept ACK from vasild who intends to review further, with no objections. The PR is fresh (opened same day), CI clean, and ready for review now, though it competes conceptually with #34707 for the same underlying problem.
